options.text: Nice uniform. Did you lose a bet?
You call this an army?
I've seen scarier scarecrows.
Do they teach you to scowl like that, or is it natural?
Your boots don't match.
Rough shave this morning?
You smell like a long campaign.
That helmet's a size too big.
Do you practice standing around, or is it a gift?
Your sergeant must be so proud.
I've met friendlier guard dogs.
How's the glamorous soldier life treating you?
Bet you drew the short straw for this post.
You look bored out of your skull.
Your generals spend men like loose change.
Digging holes and dying in them — that's the whole plan, right?
Your quota's just a butcher's bill with extra steps.
The line holds because nobody's smart enough to run.
How many of you die for each mile of mud?
All your procedures, and you still bleed like everyone else.
Do you file a form before you're allowed to think?
Your precious doctrine is just cowardice with paperwork.
Radio discipline, ration discipline — do they ration your spine too?
Your ledgers won't remember you, you know.
Hiding in the sand isn't strategy, it's cowardice.
All those proverbs, and not one straight answer in your whole camp.
Patience is what you call losing slowly.
Your mirages don't scare anyone who owns a map.
Ambush is just a coward's word for murder.
You're a disgrace to whatever mother raised you.
Your whole company isn't worth one honest farmer.
I've scraped better soldiers off my boots.
Your dead comrades would be ashamed of you.
Everyone laughs at your kind behind your back.
You're nothing but a hired thug with a flag.
Your commander is an idiot and you know it.
This land will be glad when your lot is gone.
You fight for scraps and call it honor.
I've seen deserters with more dignity.
Your cause died years ago. You're just too dumb to notice.
Cowards, all of you, dressed up as soldiers.
You take orders from fools and call it duty.
History won't even bother to forget you.
That banner of yours would make a decent floor rag.
I'd spit on your flag if it were worth the spit.
Your colors look better burning, I'd bet.
That rag on the pole — someone's laundry?
I've blown my nose on finer cloth than your banner.
Your flag stands for nothing but graves.
One day I'll take that banner home as a souvenir.
Whoever stitched your colors wasted good thread.
Keep talking and I'll shut your mouth for good.
You should sleep lightly from now on.
I know where your patrols walk. Think about that.
One day soon you'll turn around and I'll be there.
Your walls won't protect you from me.
I've buried tougher men than you.
Count your friends tonight. The number's going to shrink.
Cross me again and they'll never find you.
I could end you right here and walk away whistling.
Your kind bleeds easy. I've checked.
Tell your commander he's on my list.
Next time we meet, bring help. You'll need it.
I'm the reason soldiers pray before patrol.
Enjoy your last quiet days.
I'll burn your base down with everyone in it.
I'm going to hunt your squad down one by one.
By winter, your whole company will be bones.
I'll make your commander watch while I take everything.
Every one of you dies. I'm just deciding the order.
I'll salt your fields and poison your wells.
Your people will curse the day they took this land.
When I'm done, no one will remember your names.
Enough talk. Draw your blade.
Hit me. I dare you.
Let's settle this right now, you and me.
Come on then. Show me what your training's worth.
I'll give you the first swing. You'll need it.
Fight me, or admit you're a coward.
Your move. Or are you all talk?
Right here, right now. Let's go.
Put your hands up, soldier.
I've been itching for this all day. Come on.
Make me leave. If you can.
All of you at once. I'll wait.
Your whole squad against me. Fair fight, finally.
Every one of you cowards, come and get me!
I'll take your whole patrol apart right here.
Which of you dies first? Line up.
Your friends died easy. You will too.
I remember how the last one begged.
Want to end up like the others I put down?
How many of yours have I sent home in boxes now?
Tell the widows I said hello.
The ones I killed? They fought better than you look.
I've made a hobby of your people.
Careful. You know what happened to the last patrol that annoyed me.
Maybe I'll add you to my count today.
They give stripes to anyone these days, huh?
An officer? You? Who did you bribe?
Does the fancy plume come with a brain?
You're a grunt because thinking scared you, right?
Do they let the grunts talk, or should I find your handler?
Shopkeeper with a sword. Adorable.
Counting sacks — real hero's work.
How's the war going from behind your ledger?

negative: Funny. Write it on your ration card. Oh, wait — you don't get one.
Keep the jokes. You'll want something to say when the mood here turns.
neutral: The uniform survived three owners. Show respect for the fabric.
Bored, yes. Boredom out here is the good outcome. Don't fix it.
Ha. The scarecrows work for us too. Better hours than the infantry.
positive: From you, friend, I'll allow one joke a day. That was it. Spend tomorrow's wisely.
The helmet is big so the laughs fit inside. Old army trick.
My sergeant IS proud. Mostly of my digging. It's a narrow pride.

negative: Humor noted. Filed under provocation, minor. The file grows.
Mockery of personnel is a poor use of your remaining goodwill.
neutral: The uniform meets specification. Your opinion doesn't alter specification.
Standing here IS the job. Deterrence looks boring right up until it isn't.
If that was wit, transmission received. No further response warranted.
positive: Ha. Log that one under 'friendly banter, tolerated.' Once.
The scowl is standard issue. The smile costs extra and you haven't paid.
Careful, friend — I'm allowed exactly one joke per shift and I'm saving mine.

negative: The jester walks far from home. Jesters have accidents on long roads.
Laugh. The desert collects laughter and returns it with interest.
neutral: The camel also mocks its driver, and still it carries the load. Speak on.
A dull knife makes noise on the stone. A sharp one is quiet. Consider which you are.
My boots do not match because the road does not match. Practical, not poor.
positive: Ah, the friend arrives with thorns today. Sit; we will trade them for figs.
You smell a long campaign on me? Good nose. It was a very long campaign.
Teasing is a guest's spice, friend. A pinch flavors. A handful ruins the pot.

vengeful: You mock the line with our blood already on you. The count just grew teeth.
Say 'quota' again. I'll show you where your name fits in it.
negative: The line buried better critics than you. It has room for reviews.
We spend men, yes. We're rich in what matters. You're spending something rarer: luck.
neutral: Every mile of mud costs. We pay. That's why the mud is ours.
Smart ones run, you say. The runners are dead too, friend. At least ours died facing forward.
The plan is simple because simple survives shelling. Complicated dies with its author.
positive: From a stranger, that's spit. From you, friend, it's a bruise. Pick your words like footing.
You've eaten at our fires and you talk like the enemy's pamphlets. Disappointing.
Careful. The line forgives its friends much. Not everything.

vengeful: Doctrine mockery from a flagged killer. The recommendation on your file just changed.
Keep talking. You're writing the authorization I've been waiting for.
negative: The paperwork you mock is why our dead are few and yours will be counted precisely.
Cowardice with paperwork still holds every crossroads you need. Sit with that.
neutral: Procedure is what's standing between this conversation and a very different one.
We bleed, yes. Rarely, and on schedule, and never for free.
Your critique is noted, unsigned, and unqualified. Dismissed.
positive: That's beneath you, friend. The doctrine you mock has kept you alive in this sector twice.
I'd debate you, but insulting the manual to the man holding it is just poor tactics.
One warning, because I like you: the ledger hears everything. Even jokes.

vengeful: You call us cowards with our blood drying on your hands. The sand is done waiting.
Mock patience once more. Learn how suddenly patience ends.
negative: The map you own shows where things are. We are never where things are.
Call it hiding. The ones who called it hiding before you are under the dunes now.
neutral: The straight answer you want is a straight road. Straight roads are where ambushes live.
Losing slowly, winning slowly — the desert doesn't rush and neither does its verdict.
Murder announces itself. The ambush merely arrives. Words matter less than outcomes.
positive: From a friend, that thorn goes deeper. Pull it back out, and we will call it the wind talking.
You have sat in our shade and now you spit toward it. The shade notices, friend.
Even the fig tree drops one bitter fruit. I will assume that was yours.

vengeful: Loud words from a debtor. Your account with the line is overdrawn and collections are near.
Insulting the dead's comrades, with your record. Even the crows are embarrassed for you.
negative: Keep going. Every word makes the eventual arithmetic easier to enjoy.
The line has been called worse by artillery. But artillery could back it up.
neutral: Hm. Words are cheap. Ours are cheaper: leave.
You insult a wall. The wall stands. That's the whole exchange.
Brave mouth, unescorted body. Rare combination. Usually brief.
positive: That's how you talk to us now? The mud remembers who it warmed, friend.
The line took you for a friend. Friends get one such sentence free. It's spent.

vengeful: Verbal hostility from a red-flagged subject. You are assembling your own case file.
Every insult is logged. The log is nearly thick enough to act on. Continue.
negative: Slander of personnel: recorded. Response: pending. Behavior: yours to correct.
You mistake restraint for weakness. Restraint is a setting. It changes.
neutral: Opinion registered. Its influence on anything: zero.
This command has survived sieges. It will survive your vocabulary.
Insulting the garrison at the garrison. Bold logistics on your part.
positive: That's a strange way to thank the people who keep your roads open, friend.
I'll assume a bad day and delete the transmission. Once.

vengeful: Loud insults from a marked man. The desert has heard your voice. It can find it again.
Spend your words, killer. They are the last coins in your purse.
negative: The dog barks at the caravan. The caravan does not vote on it.
Your tongue digs quickly. Tongues make poor shovels and worse graves.
neutral: Wind through a tent flap. Loud, brief, forgotten by morning.
We are called cowards by everyone we outlive. It is a long, quiet list.
Honor, scraps — name them as you like. We eat, we endure, we remain.
positive: A friend's insult cuts with a familiar knife. Sheathe it, and we will drink to forgetting.
The kettle has poured for you, and this is the toast you bring? Try again, friend.

vengeful: That banner wrapped our dead — the ones you made. Touch it with one more word.
Mock the colors, blood-debtor, and the quota closes around your name today.
negative: Men froze holding that rag so you could sneer at it. They'd trade places with you gladly.
The banner's seen shellfire. Your opinion registers somewhat lower.
neutral: Careful. Cloth is cheap. What it's soaked in isn't.
Laundry, ha. It's washed in worse than soap, friend. Walk away from this topic.
positive: Even in jest, not the banner. That's the one wire you don't test with us.
The thread you mock stitched shrouds too. Change the subject while it's still changeable.

vengeful: Desecration talk from a hostile-flagged subject. You are volunteering for consequences.
The colors you threaten fly over people authorized to answer threats. Recall that.
negative: That standard represents the command structure. Contempt for it is contempt logged at the top.
Souvenir. Noted. Attempts on regimental colors carry the maximum response. All of it.
neutral: The flag is inventory, the meaning isn't. Insult neither on this ground.
Colors stay up through worse weather than sarcasm.
positive: Friend, there are jokes we trade and jokes we don't. The colors head the second list.
I'd let that pass, but the flag outranks us both. Retract it.

vengeful: Our banner shaded the graves you dug for us. Spit, and join what you planted.
The cloth you mock has your name sewn in it now. Thread pulls both ways.
negative: The banner survived three empires of better insults. It will outlast your mouth.
Burn our colors? Fire is our cousin. It knows whose side it sleeps on.
neutral: The cloth is old because nothing has managed to take it down. Meditate on that.
You call it a rag. Rags wipe up spills. Ours has wiped up armies.
positive: Not the banner, friend. Even the shade has bones, and you just stepped on one.
The weaver of those colors fed you last month. Swallow the joke with her bread.

vengeful: Say it. Give me the excuse. The shovels are already warm.
Threats, from you, with the count where it stands? The line was hoping you'd say that.
negative: You threaten a trench system, alone, in the open. Poets die like this too.
Sleep lightly, he says. We haven't slept since the war started. Your move was pre-owned.
neutral: Threats are a loan against your future. The line always collects.
Noted. Filed between the weather and the lice as things that might kill us.
You know where our patrols walk? Good. They'll know where you sleep. Fair trade.
positive: Threatening us, friend? The mud between us must mean less to you than it does to us.
That word choice costs you warmth at our fires. Keep spending and see.

vengeful: Threat received from flagged subject. Weapons posture updating. Final chance to retract.
You just met the threshold. What happens next is procedure, not anger.
negative: Threat logged verbatim. Response authorization is now one signature away.
You've threatened a garrisoned force with a knife and confidence. The math is public.
neutral: That statement meets the definition of a threat. Definitions have consequences here.
Your list, your promises — all transcribed. Aegis archives outlive their subjects.
Advisory: threatening a soldier at his post is the fastest downgrade available.
positive: From a friendly, that's either a bad joke or a worse decision. Clarify. Now.
I'll mark it as stress and strike it. The second one stands forever.

vengeful: Threaten us again. The sand under you is already listening for the fall.
Good. Announce yourself. The trap prefers informed guests.
negative: You threaten the desert's own. The desert heard. It is very good at waiting.
Loud promises travel far here. So do we, and more quietly.
neutral: Men who tell the scorpion their plans make the scorpion's work simple.
Your last quiet days, ours — the desert decides whose. It has never once consulted a threat.
We will not find you, you say? We do not find people. People arrive at us.
positive: A threat from a friend is a crack in a water jar. Mend it now, while the water remains.
The shade withdraws from words like those. Feel the sun on your neck? Choose again.

vengeful: Burn our base? You'll be part of the foundation before the first spark.
The order of who dies is set, debtor. You wrote yourself to the top just now.
negative: Whole companies have promised us bones. We compost promises out here.
Salt our fields? We farm mud and casualties. You can't poison what's already bitter.
neutral: That's not a threat, it's a confession with a delivery date. The line will be waiting.
Big words. The winter you promise us has tried every year. We're still here to shovel it.
positive: You'd say that to us? Then the friendship was ration paper. It burns fast.
The line just moved you from one list to the other. There's no third list.

vengeful: Mass-casualty threat, on record, from a known hostile. Restraint is now rescinded.
You've stated intent to destroy this command. Doctrine has one page for that. Short page.
negative: That statement upgrades you to a strategic concern. Strategic concerns get resolved.
Threats against the installation trigger standing orders. They do not expire and do not forgive.
neutral: You just described a war crime to a witness in uniform. The report writes itself.
Noted, escalated, and flagged at command level. Your name now briefs generals.
positive: Whatever trust existed is administratively void. Effective immediately.
That sentence ends every courtesy this sector owed you. Confirmed and logged.

vengeful: Poison our wells? The wells already whisper your name. Water has a long memory.
Speak of our deaths once more and the dune will speak of yours first.
negative: You threaten fire in a land of sand. We have hosted fire before. It left hungry.
Curse the day, curse the land — the desert has swallowed louder curses with its breakfast.
neutral: No one remembers our names now, walker. That is the entire trick. You threaten smoke.
Your promise is large. The desert measures men against it while they sleep.
positive: So the guest burns the tent in his heart. The shade hears, friend, and the shade withdraws.
Between us there was tea and salt. You have poured out both. What remains is the desert.

vengeful: Finally. The count settles today.
You asked. The line answers.
negative: Fine. One more for the quota.
Short fight. Long ditch.
neutral: So be it. Dig your own after.
The mud takes everyone eventually. You've just volunteered early.
Wrong trench to spit into.
positive: So the friend wants the shovel's edge. Grief later. Work now.
You were one of ours in everything but the ledger. The ledger wins.

vengeful: Weapons-free. At last.
Authorization: granted. By you.
negative: Contact is now kinetic. Copy.
You initiated. The report will read exactly that.
neutral: Compliance failed. Engaging.
ROE satisfied. Regrettable. Proceeding.
This was avoidable. Was.
positive: Friendly status revoked. Engaging under protest — but engaging.
You forced the one order I hoped to never file on you.

vengeful: The debt collects itself now.
The sand opens. In you go.
negative: As the fool insists, the desert obliges.
You called for the storm. It was already behind you.
neutral: So the moth demands the flame. Granted.
The blade regrets nothing. Neither shall I.
You chose the short story. It ends here.
positive: You break the salt between us. The pieces are sharp. Feel them.
The shade loved you, friend. The shade will still bury you.

vengeful: All of us at once — the only prayer of yours we'll answer.
The whole line heard the debtor volunteer. Take him.
negative: The whole section? Lads, we've been challenged by a hero. Bury him with honors.
You counted us and still spoke. Arithmetic was never your friend.
neutral: Squad — up. The gentleman insists.
One against the line. The line accepts. The line always accepts.
positive: You'd raise your hand against all of us who fed you? Then all of us answer.
The whole line mourns what you were. Briefly. Boys — shovels down, blades out.

vengeful: Section: weapons-free on the flagged subject. Execute.
All units, hostile confirmed by his own transmission. Engage.
negative: Squad, form on me. The subject has requested a demonstration. Provide it.
You challenged a fire team, alone. This will be brief and well-documented.
neutral: All stations: contact initiated by subject. Weapons out. Engage.
One man, whole squad. Doctrine has a word for this: cleanup.
positive: Team — former friendly has gone hostile by declaration. Standard response. Go.
Every courtesy is now void, and every blade here is on duty. You chose the audience.

vengeful: Brothers — the marked one calls for us all. The sand agrees. Take him.
He shouts at the whole desert. Show him how much desert there is.
negative: You challenge everyone in the shade at once. The shade empties. Behind you.
Riders — the loud one has invited the entire night. Deliver it.
neutral: One voice against many knives. The proverb ends the usual way. Come, all of you.
The whole camp heard the invitation. The whole camp arrives.
positive: He turns on every hand that poured for him. Then every hand answers. Rise.
You were a friend to each of us, and you spit at all of us. All of us reply, then.

vengeful: You joke about our dead to my face. Reach for anything. Please.
Eleven names, and now comedy. The twelfth entry is standing very close to me.
negative: The boxes you brag about — we carried them. Remember that when the dark comes for you.
Keep the widows out of your mouth or lose the mouth.
neutral: Boasting about our dead is one wire past clever. Step back over it.
The count between us was cooling. You just blew on the coals. Your funeral. Possibly literally.
They fought better than I look? They taught me. Come find out how well.
positive: You'd mock the graves and drink at our fire? Pick one. Forever.
The line was learning to forget your debt. It just relearned it, word for word.

vengeful: You are confessing to casualties, in uniform hearing, with a smile. Perfect testimony.
One more sentence about our dead and doctrine handles the punctuation.
negative: Casualty mockery from their killer. The file is now a case. Cases close.
Names, dates, next of kin — we have them all memorized. Your jokes are evidence.
neutral: Those personnel had records, families, and comrades on this wall. Choose your next words.
Bragging about kills to the deceased's unit. Tactically illiterate. Morally worse.
Your count is accurate. So is ours. Ours includes projections.
positive: We rebuilt trust over those graves and you dance on them. Rebuild is cancelled.
That was the sentence that ends the ledger's patience. Logged as final.

vengeful: You laugh over our dead. Their sand is under your boots right now. Feel it shifting?
The begging you remember — the desert remembers differently. Ask it tonight.
negative: Mock the graves and the graves grow curious about you.
Every name you took has kin in this shade. You are performing for the bereaved.
neutral: The dead you count were sons of the dune. The dune counts also, and it is patient.
Your hobby, as you call it, has a membership fee. The desert is drafting the bill.
Careful. Grief here does not weep. It sharpens.
positive: We forgave the blood, friend, and you make songs of it. The forgiveness is leaving the tent.
You joke about wounds we let heal in your favor. Watch them reopen toward you.

negative: The stripes came off dead men's sleeves. Want to see how they're earned back?
Mock the rank, meet the rank's job. It involves you regretting things.
neutral: Stripes mean I count the dead instead of joining them. Promotion of a sort.
The grunt hears you fine. The grunt outlived three clever talkers this month.
I keep the sacks counted so the line keeps eating. Insult me after you've missed a meal.
positive: Ha — bribed with what? Nobody's paid the line since autumn. It's pure stubbornness up here.
Careful, friend, the ledger and the shovel are the same weight in my hands.
The plume was my predecessor's. The brain is my own. Both survived him. One will survive you.

negative: That rank clears me to make your afternoon procedurally unpleasant. Test it.
Mocking the chain of command, at a checkpoint, alone. Your risk assessment is broken.
neutral: The commission is earned through boards and battlefields. Your comedy, through neither.
Grunts execute the plan. Executing is the part that matters. Note the word.
Supply is the arm that decides whether the other arms lift. Mind the shopkeeper.
positive: The plume is regulation, the brain passed selection, and the friend is on thin ice. Ha.
Careful — this ledger has a line item for 'attitude.' Yours is trending expensive.
I'll take 'shopkeeper with a sword.' It's accurate, and the sword half is the operative half.

negative: You mock the hand that assigns the night watches. Enjoy the watches it assigns you.
The quartermaster you tease decides who eats. Reflect, hungrily.
neutral: Rank here is not stripes. It is how many storms you have read correctly. I am owed many.
The grunt, as you say, is the finger on the desert's hand. Fingers close.
I count sacks, yes. Also debts, insults, and exits. Three ledgers, one pen.
positive: Ha — the plume is for the falcon, friend. She outranks us both and knows it.
Tease gently. The man behind the ledger sets the guest portions, and memory seasons them.
My stripes are sun-lines and scar-lines. The promotion board was the desert itself.
